title: Network Recovery Pathways
summary: Given a directed acyclic graph with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where edges[i] = [ui, vi, costi] represent a one-way communication from node ui to vi with a recovery cost of costi, and a boolean array online indicating which nodes are online, find the maximum path score.
statement: Given a directed acyclic graph with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where edges[i] = [ui, vi, costi] represent a one-way communication from node ui to vi with a recovery cost of costi, and a boolean array online indicating which nodes are online, find the maximum path score. A path from node 0 to n-1 is valid if all intermediate nodes are online and the total recovery cost does not exceed k. The path score is the minimum edge cost on the path. Return -1 if no valid path exists.
constraints: The directed graph is acyclic with up to 50,000 nodes and 100,000 edges.
Only paths through online nodes are valid; endpoints are always online.
Total edge cost must not exceed k; maximize the minimum edge cost or return -1.
hints: Requiring every edge to meet a score threshold turns the objective into a monotone feasibility question.
Binary search the score; for each threshold, find the cheapest path using qualifying online edges.
Keep edges with cost at least the threshold and run Dijkstra, accepting destination cost at most k.
A feasible score implies every lower score is feasible, and shortest-path cost exactly tests the budget.
editorial: A feasible score implies every lower score is feasible, and shortest-path cost exactly tests the budget.

tests.explanation: Only the route with edge costs three and four fits the budget, scoring three.
The online path through node two scores six.
